summary: Bollinger Bands show no edge for buying dips on these pairs. On BTC, ETH and SOL, price crossing back up through the lower band, or sitting below it, did no better than a random candle on 1h, 4h or daily. The result that holds up is a short on 4h: entries as price crossed back down through the upper band did 0.51% worse than random after 20 candles, and the gap holds without its strongest stretch.

verdicts.use: Buying the dip at the lower band
verdicts.text: On 1h, 4h and daily, a cross up through the lower band did no better than random entries. Being below the band, or a cross up through the 2.5 SD band, did no better either.

verdicts.use: Going long on a break above the upper band
verdicts.text: On 4h, price moved more after these candles than after random ones, in a window where price rose. These candles fire in volatile stretches, so this is timing, not a direction call, and it vanishes without Aug 10–17, 2021. On 1h and daily, it showed nothing.

verdicts.use: Shorting a cross back down through the upper band
verdicts.text: Worse than random on 4h, and it holds without its strongest stretch. On 1h and daily the pooled result sits inside the luck band.

verdicts.use: Going long on a cross up through the middle band
verdicts.text: No better than random entries on 1h, 4h or daily.

notes: On 1h, price crossing up the lower band gave 5,018 entries in 2,653 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.03% ahead of random entries, inside the luck band. Being below the band gives about twice as many entries and lands in the same place. The 2.5 SD band gives about half as many crosses and also shows nothing. None of the three showed anything in uptrends or in downtrends.

On 4h, price crossing up the upper band was followed by moves 0.51% above random entries after 20 candles, just above the luck band. These candles cluster in volatile stretches, and in a window where price rose they caught bigger moves because of when they fired, not because they picked direction. The gap vanishes without Aug 10–17, 2021. In uptrends it reached 0.71% and held without that stretch and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles, again a sign of timing in a rising window. In downtrends it showed nothing.

Shorting as price crossed back down through the upper band on 4h did 0.51% worse than random entries after 20 candles. It holds without its strongest stretch and shows again at 100 candles, though not at 10 or 50. In uptrends the result rests on Aug 10–17, 2021 and is gone without it. In downtrends it showed nothing. On daily the same short is inside the band pooled, but in downtrends it beat random by 5.16% after 20 days, over 45 separate moves. That held without its strongest entry and showed at 50 and 100 candles.

Single stretches can fake a result. On daily, SOL's long on an upper-band break beat random by 11%, but only because of signals between Jan 30, 2021 and Feb 22, 2021, when SOL rose and those volatile candles caught the move. ETH's daily cross up through the lower band did 5.96% worse, and that rests on signals between Jan 21, 2026 and Feb 6, 2026. The 2.5 SD cross on daily in downtrends did 5.28% worse only because of May 1–12, 2022, during the Terra collapse. The 4h middle-band cross in downtrends was 0.39% ahead, but only because of Jan 11–12, 2023.

For a long DCA bot, a lower-band start condition adds nothing on these pairs. The DCA orders and take profit decide the result. A short bot that opens as price slips back under the upper band on 4h is trading against continuation, so leave that trigger out or gate it behind a downtrend filter. Treat an upper-band break on 4h as a volatility marker next to your own trend condition, not as a direction call. It breaks down when the market goes sideways or falls.
